# Objective Truth Must Be Something Non-Utilitarian

This pragmatist talk about truths in the plural, about their utility and satisfactoriness, about the success with which they 'work,' etc., suggests to the typical intellectualist mind a sort of coarse lame second-rate makeshift article of truth.[^1] Such truths are not real truth.[^2] Such tests are merely subjective.[^3] As against this, objective truth must be something non-utilitarian, haughty, refined, remote, august, exalted.[^4] It must be an absolute correspondence of our thoughts with an equally absolute reality.[^5] It must be what we OUGHT to think, unconditionally.[^6] The conditioned ways in which we DO think are so much irrelevance and matter for psychology.[^7] Down with psychology, up with logic, in all this question![^8]

[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It must be an absolute correspondence of our thoughts with an equally absolute reality."
